counting_conventions.dia-api: Distinct public/protected member names per export class in types/dia.d.ts via the TypeScript AST (generic methods and required properties included, [Symbol.iterator] included); overloads collapsed; private and underscore-prefixed excluded; inherited members counted on the declaring class only; plus the namespace enums CellView.Highlighting, ElementView.Flags, LinkView.Flags, Paper.sorting, Paper.Layers (one entry per enum).
counting_conventions.paper-option: Declared property fields of the Paper.Options interface in types/dia.d.ts via AST; inherited mvc.ViewOptions fields excluded.
counting_conventions.event: Union of dia.Paper.EventMap keys, trigger() literals in src/**, and dynamic change:/eventPrefix patterns (flagged dynamic).
counting_conventions.router: Keys of RouterArgumentsMap in types/routers.d.ts, plus routers.rightAngle.Directions (RightAngleDirections enum, one entry).
counting_conventions.connector: Keys of ConnectorArgumentsMap in types/connectors.d.ts, plus connectors.curve.Directions and connectors.curve.TangentDirections (one entry per enum).
counting_conventions.link-anchor: Exported anchor names in src/linkAnchors/index.mjs (resolveRef helper excluded).
counting_conventions.highlighter: export const names in src/highlighters/*.mjs, plus declared members of the highlighter classes and the list.Directions/list.Positions enums in types/highlighters.d.ts.
counting_conventions.link-tool: Export classes in types/linkTools.d.ts (top-level plus nested handle classes such as Vertices.VertexHandle), plus their declared members (constructors excluded).
counting_conventions.element-tool: Export classes in types/elementTools.d.ts (top-level plus nested classes), plus their declared members (constructors excluded).
counting_conventions.shape: export class names in types/shapes-standard.d.ts (standard.*), plus their declared members (e.g. Cylinder.topRy; constructors excluded).
counting_conventions.layout-port: export var names under the Port namespace of types/layout.d.ts.
counting_conventions.layout-port-label: export var names under the PortLabel namespace of types/layout.d.ts.
counting_conventions.geometry: Distinct declared member names per export class in types/geometry.d.ts via AST, plus the g.Segment interface members, the g.types enum (one entry), standalone functions and bezier/scale/intersection namespace members.
counting_conventions.vectorizer: VElement member names plus VStatic interface members (prefix V.) and the V callable signature, in types/vectorizer.d.ts via AST.
counting_conventions.util: export function/var names in types/util.d.ts, including timing/interpolate/filter/format namespace members.
counting_conventions.mvc: Distinct declared member names per export class in types/mvc.d.ts via AST, plus Data (with its JS methods has/create/get/set/remove) and the single $ facade entry from src/mvc/index.mjs.
counting_conventions.presentation-attribute: Top-level keys of the attribute namespaces in src/dia/attributes/*.mjs, plus bracket-assigned aliases (ref-d, ref-points, at-connection-*, refX/refY/ref-*2/ref-r), the calc evaluator (evalAttributes, evalAttribute), use-no-break-space, the five CellView selector attributes (event, magnet, magnetSelector, highlighterSelector, containerSelector) and the props shorthand.
counting_conventions.core-config: Keys of src/config/index.mjs, plus env.addTest, env.test, setTheme, version.
counting_conventions.alg: The exported rightAnglePath function of types/alg.d.ts (upstream-flagged internal).
counting_conventions.package: Directories of packages/* in the monorepo carrying a package.json.
counting_conventions.package-api: Entry-point exports per package (see the enumerate.mjs header), including @joint/router-avoid RouterService with its members and events and the @joint/react subpath ./internal; @joint/core excluded.
counting_conventions.catalog-app: Rows of jointjs_apps_and_recipes in docs/graph-dataviz-reference-catalog.json (186 rows tracked; the 109 JointJS+ rows are greenfield GD-M5-APPS tracking excluded from the parity denominator).

entries.name: rightAnglePath
entries.behaviour: `alg.rightAnglePath` (upstream-flagged internal, consumed by @joint/router-avoid): given the two path ends with their bounding boxes, margins and exit sides, it computes the right-angled path points between them, including any required detour around an end's box.
entries.acceptance: Differential geometry oracle for `rightAnglePath`: run identical fixed inputs (boxes, points, vertices, options from the behaviour contract, including its stated defaults and rounding rule) through JointJS (@joint/core 4.3.3) and our implementation; assert returned points/path samples match under the per-function tolerance of the spec harness section (the function's own rounding reproduced first, residual <=1e-6 world units; integers exact), including one rotated-element case and one degenerate coincident-points case.

proof.note: No analogue in diagram-canvas; the README section at this line lists the uncovered areas.

entries.name: bottom
entries.behaviour: Element anchor `bottom`: input is the end element/port geometry, the magnet shape descriptor and a reference point (plus this anchor's options); output is the link end point on the element. Moving, resizing or rotating the element moves the computed point by the same rule.

entries.name: anchor
entries.behaviour: Connection point `anchor`: input is the link end segment and the end element's shape/bounding box; output trims or extends the rendered path end so the visible path starts or ends exactly at the computed boundary point (stroke and offset options honoured as declared).

entries.name: curve
entries.behaviour: Connector `curve`: input is source point, target point, routed vertices and this connector's options; output is the connection path (serialised SVG path upstream; sampled polyline/curve points on our stack). Catmull-Rom through [sourcePoint, ...route, targetPoint] converted to cubic Beziers. Defaults: direction=auto, precision=3, distanceCoefficient (coeff)=0.6, angleTangentCoefficient=80, tension (tau)=0.5; end tangents lengthen by (angle-pi/4)*80 when the end direction deviates more than 45 degrees. The Path is rounded to precision=3; raw=true returns the Path, otherwise its serialised string. curve.Directions={auto,horizontal,vertical,closest-point,outwards}; curve.TangentDirections adds {up,down,left,right}.
entries.acceptance: Differential geometry oracle for `curve`: run identical fixed inputs (boxes, points, vertices, options from the behaviour contract, including its stated defaults and rounding rule) through JointJS (@joint/core 4.3.3) and our implementation; assert returned points/path samples match under the per-function tolerance of the spec harness section (the function's own rounding reproduced first, residual <=1e-6 world units; integers exact), including one rotated-element case and one degenerate coincident-points case.

proof.note: graph edge-geometry supports an arc curve mode over known positions; JointJS curve tangents and direction options have no counterpart, so the analogue is partial.

entries.name: straight
entries.behaviour: Connector `straight`: input is source point, target point, routed vertices and this connector's options; output is the connection path (serialised SVG path upstream; sampled polyline/curve points on our stack). Connects [sourcePoint, ...routePoints, targetPoint]. Defaults: cornerType=point (plain polyline), cornerRadius=10, cornerPreserveAspectRatio=false, precision=1, raw=false. entries.name: addTo
entries.behaviour: `dia.Cell.addTo` (method). Declared as: `addTo(graph: Graph, opt?: Graph.Options): this;`. Observable contract: the inputs, return value, thrown/rejected cases and emitted change notifications are those of the declared signature; mutable model members mutate the owning graph/cell state, accessors report it without side effects beyond the documented caching.
entries.acceptance: Differential model oracle for `Cell.addTo` (addTo(graph: Graph, opt?: Graph.Options): this;): apply the same operation sequence to a JointJS graph and to our diagram-core state (via transactions with the JointJS-to-Effect projection of the spec); assert the serialised model, the returned value or rejection and the projected effect/event sequence match, including one invalid-input case that must be rejected without partial state change.

proof.note: diagram-core holds the semantic document (entities, relations, ports, views, occurrences) and applies 18 transactional commands with inverses; JointJS Cell attribute bags, embedding, and view geometry have no one-to-one counterpart, so every model member is at most partial.

entries.name: set
entries.behaviour: `mvc.Collection.set` (method). Declared as: `set(models?: Array<{} | TModel>, options?: CollectionSetOptions): TModel[];`. The set method performs a "smart" update of the collection with the passed list of models. If a model in the list isn't yet in the collection it will be added; if the model is already in the collection its attributes will be merged; and if the collection contains any models that aren't present in the list, they'll be removed. All of the appropriate "add", "remove", and "change" events are fired as this happens. Returns the touched models in the collection. entries.behaviour: `@joint/router-avoid` `RouterService.destroy` (method). entries.acceptance: Differential rendering oracle for `x-alignment`: create the same cell JSON in JointJS and in our implementation; assert the model echo, the computed geometry (within 1e-6 world units after the stated rounding) and, where pixels are compared, the golden capture within the harness tolerance; text cases use the shared fitted-label measurement and the multi-line breakText contract.

proof.note: No module owns this on our stack yet; a new module is required (see the spec).

entries.name: manhattan
entries.behaviour: Router `manhattan`: input is the link source anchor, target anchor and current intermediate vertices plus this router's options; output is the replacement intermediate-vertex list, in order, through which the rendered connection must pass. A* search on a step grid (step=10, maximumLoops=2000, precision=1) with maxAllowedDirectionChange=90, perpendicular=true, excludeEnds=[], excludeTypes=[], start/end directions [top,right,bottom,left]; returned vertices are grid-aligned and rounded to precision=1.
entries.acceptance: Differential geometry oracle for `manhattan`: run identical fixed inputs (boxes, points, vertices, options from the behaviour contract, including its stated defaults and rounding rule) through JointJS (@joint/core 4.3.3) and our implementation; assert returned points/path samples match under the per-function tolerance of the spec harness section (the function's own rounding reproduced first, residual <=1e-6 world units; integers exact), including one rotated-element case and one degenerate coincident-points case.

proof.note: No analogue in diagram-canvas; the README section at this line lists the uncovered areas.

entries.name: metro
entries.behaviour: Router `metro`: input is the link source anchor, target anchor and current intermediate vertices plus this router's options; output is the replacement intermediate-vertex list, in order, through which the rendered connection must pass. Delegates to manhattan with maxAllowedDirectionChange=45 and 8 search directions (4 orthogonal + 4 diagonal); diagonal step cost is ceil(sqrt(2*step^2)); on exceeding maximumLoops or an inaccessible target the octilinear fallbackRoute (single 45-degree bend through rounded points, obstacles ignored) is returned. Rounding follows manhattan (precision=1, points rounded).
entries.acceptance: Differential geometry oracle for `metro`: run identical fixed inputs (boxes, points, vertices, options from the behaviour contract, including its stated defaults and rounding rule) through JointJS (@joint/core 4.3.3) and our implementation; assert returned points/path samples match under the per-function tolerance of the spec harness section (the function's own rounding reproduced first, residual <=1e-6 world units; integers exact), including one rotated-element case and one degenerate coincident-points case.

proof.note: graph render-geometry implements an octilinear (45-degree) edge route and a metro layout; it is a per-edge render style over known positions, not a per-link router over anchors and vertices, so the analogue is partial.
